handoff.purpose: Define patch digest, truncation, record/load attempts, and sample inspirations.

symbols.name: digest_patch
symbols.note: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of encoded patch bytes.

symbols.name: _truncate
symbols.note: Truncates text to limit, keeping tail if over limit; prepends '...'.

symbols.name: record_attempt
symbols.note: Appends one JSONL line to path; creates parent dirs; returns truncated Attempt.

symbols.name: load_attempts
symbols.note: Reads JSONL file, skips unparseable lines, returns tuple of Attempt; never raises.

symbols.name: sample_inspirations
symbols.note: Samples attempts with deduplication by digest; excludes exclude_digest; outcome diversity not enforced in visible code.

claims.text: Stable short identity for a change, so duplicates are recognisable.
claims.why: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256; deterministic and short.

claims.text: Two candidates that produced byte-identical changes are the same attempt for inspiration purposes, and saying so costs 16 hex characters instead of a diff.
claims.why: Digest length is 16 hex chars; identical patches produce same digest.

claims.text: Keep the TAIL: a traceback's last lines carry the actual error, and the head is import noise.
claims.why: Truncation keeps the tail by taking last (limit-3) characters.

claims.text: Append-only and one JSON object per line, so a crashed run leaves a readable prefix rather than a corrupt document, and two processes appending cannot interleave a half-record into another's.
claims.why: Uses 'a' mode; writes single JSON line per call. OS append is atomic for small writes on most systems.

claims.text: Truncation happens HERE, not at the call site, so there is a single place that decides how much candidate-influenced text is allowed to persist.
claims.why: Calls _truncate on summary and limits unfixed to 20; no truncation elsewhere visible.
Catches OSError and returns empty tuple; catches ValueError/TypeError/AttributeError per line.

claims.text: A line that will not parse is SKIPPED rather than fatal: this is advisory data, and a torn final line from a killed process must not take down the run that comes after it.
claims.why: Skips lines that raise (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) during json.loads or Attempt.from_dict.

claims.text: Pick a few prior attempts worth showing the next one.
claims.why: The docstring describes intent; actual selection logic not fully visible (no sorting or diversity enforcement shown).

claims.text: Adapted from upstream database.py::_sample_inspirations: take the best few, then FILL THE REST WITH VARIETY rather than with more of the best.
claims.why: Upstream reference not available; variety logic not implemented in visible code (no outcome-based filtering).

claims.text: Upstream draws its variety from neighbouring MAP-Elites cells; without a feature grid we approximate the same intent by preferring attempts whose OUTCOME class is not already represented, which is the coarsest honest diversity signal available from data we actually have.
claims.why: No outcome-based filtering visible in this chunk; claim about diversity signal not implemented here.

claims.text: DEDUPLICATION BY DIGEST. Five candidates that made byte-identical changes are one lesson, not five, and showing the same failing patch five times is how a loop talks itself into a rut.
claims.why: Uses 'seen' set to skip attempts with duplicate patch_digest; excludes exclude_digest.

claims.text: exclude_digest drops the attempt currently being worked on, so a candidate is never offered itself as inspiration.
claims.why: Initializes seen with exclude_digest if non-empty.

claims.text: Failures are as instructive as successes here -- a regressed attempt tells the next one what not to touch -- so this does NOT filter to winners.
claims.why: No filtering based on outcome visible; all attempts added to pool.

claims.text: Ordering is best-first and fully deterministic given rng.
claims.why: No sorting visible; pool order depends on input iteration. rng used only for random seeding, not for ordering.

observations.what: digest_patch returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256; deterministic.
_truncate keeps tail when text exceeds limit; prepends '...'.
record_attempt writes one JSONL line; creates parent dirs; truncates summary and unfixed.
load_attempts never raises; skips unparseable lines; returns empty tuple if file missing or unreadable.
sample_inspirations deduplicates by patch_digest; excludes exclude_digest; no outcome-based diversity or sorting visible.
